speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been persisting and if you have noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome with Diarrhea (IBS-D).

The patient's symptoms of chronic diarrhea, relief of pain with defecation, and urgency are classic for IBS. However, the history of mucus and the recent exposure at a campsite raises concern for an infectious etiology or inflammatory bowel disease. I will request a Stool_Culture and Ova_and_Parasites test to rule out infection and a C-Reactive Protein to assess for inflammation.
